newsitem.title: INDIA: ANZ to raise $300 mln for India Haldia Petrochem.
newsitem.headline: ANZ to raise $300 mln for India Haldia Petrochem.

text.p: ANZ Investment Bank said it had been appointed arranger for a $300 million offshore loan to be raised by Haldia Petrochemicals Ltd, a proposed naphtha-based petrochemical plant in eastern India.
The borrowing will be structured in two tranches, it said.
The frist tranche, of up to $150 million, would be backed by deferred payment guarantees to be provided by Indian financial institutions/banks.
Another $150 million would be a commercial loan with limited recourse to the project.

The $1.4 billion project has a debt-equity ratio of 1.6 to one. The company is sponsored by the West Bengal Industrial Development Corporation, the Chatterjee Petrochem (Mauritius) Company and the House of Tatas represented by Tata Engineering and Locomotive Company Ltd and Tata Electric Cos.
ANZ said the project was in an advanced stage.
It said all the process licensers have been selected and the firm has completed the basic engineering of all process units.

U.S. firm Bechtel has been appointed overall project management contractor. Haldia Petrochemicals has secured approximately $375 million equivalent in loans from Indian financial institutions and banks and about $127 million in export credit from Japan's Export-Import Bank and is "at an advanced stage in securing other loans and guarantees from other domestic and international financial instititutions and banks."
ANZ said the sponsors have already subscribed to 51 percent of the total equity requirement of about $550 million.
The bank did not say when the loan issue would be launched.
